NASHR:v2p310/r19.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p310/r19.speaker: أبو جعفر وعاصم وروح
NASHR:v2p310/r19.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, ʿĀṣim, and Rawḥ open both consonants in thamar; Ruways agrees in the first occurrence only.
NASHR:v2p310/r19.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر وعاصم وروح بفتح الثاء والميم، وافقهم رويس في الأول

NASHR:v2p310/r20.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p310/r20.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p310/r20.claim: Abu ʿAmr uses damma on the tha and sukun on the mim in both occurrences.
NASHR:v2p310/r20.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بضم الثاء، وإسكان الميم فيهما

NASHR:v2p310/r21.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p310/r21.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p310/r21.claim: The remaining readers put damma on both the tha and mim in both occurrences.
NASHR:v2p310/r21.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بضم الثاء والميم في الموضعين

DAMGHANI:v1p146/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r9.claim: Iḥāṭa can mean destruction: a person is destroyed by his associationism, and the garden’s fruit perishes.
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r9.anchor: الثالث : الإحاطة الإهلاك قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p91#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p91#2/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p91#2/r2.claim: In one Qur'anic use, أصبح means that morning arrived; the source groups the cave-garden and Qalam passages under this sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p91#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما : إدراك الصباح للصبح . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف : ﴿ فأصبح يقلب كفيه ﴾

BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r4.claim: The threatened disaster occurs: the two gardens and all their contents are destroyed; being surrounded by an enemy conveys being overcome and ruined.
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r4.anchor: مأخوذ من أحاط به العدو لأنه إذا أحاط به فقد غلبه واستولى عليه

BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r5.claim: Turning the palms over expresses regret and grief, as a regretful person commonly strikes one hand against the other.
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r5.anchor: ظهرا لبطن تأسفا وتحسرا كما هو عادة النادمين

BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r6.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r6.claim: The gestures of turning the palms, biting the hand or fingertips, and gnashing the teeth are metonymies for regret because they accompany it.
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r6.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" تقليب الكفين وعض الكف والأنامل

BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r7.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r7.claim: A cited couplet says that grieving over what has passed is wrong because what is gone will not return and remembering it is futile.

BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r8.claim: His regret is expressed over the money spent cultivating the garden; sorrow over voluntary spending can stand for sorrow over the garden obtained with it.
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r8.anchor: ولعل تخصيص الندم به دون ما هلك الآن من الجنة لما أنه إنما يكون على الأفعال الاختيارية

BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r9.claim: The grape garden is empty and collapsed: its vine supports fell, and the vines fell over them; it is singled out as the principal asset.
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r9.anchor: أي : الجنة من الأعناب المحفوفة بنخل

BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r10.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r10.claim: One account says God sent fire that burned the garden and its water sank away.
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r10.anchor: قيل أرسل الله عليها نارا فأحرقتها وغار ماؤها

BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r11.claim: The owner recalls his brother's admonition and realizes that associating partners with God caused his ruin; wishing for faith now is not sincere repentance because he wanted faith for worldly gain.
BURSEVI:v5p191#4/r11.anchor: كأنه تذكر موعظة أخيه وعلم أنه إنما أتي من جهة الشرك

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223#2/r1.claim: The ḍamma-on-both-vowels form treats ثمره as a plural of a plural; fatḥa treats it as a collective whose singular takes tāʾ; ḍamma plus sukūn derives it from investment of wealth.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223#2/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن ضمهما أنه جعله جمع الجمع والحجة لمن فتحهما أنه جعله من الجمع

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223#2/r2.claim: In لكن هو الله ربي, the written alif reflects لكن أنا after hamza deletion and nūn assimilation; readers omitting it in liaison rely on the nūn's fatḥa, while retaining it at pause follows the script.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223#2/r2.anchor: فالحجة لمن أثبتها أن الأصل فيه لكن أنا فحذفت الهمزة تخفيفا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads ثمر and بثمره with ḍamma on thāʾ and sukūn on mīm; some transmissions from him match Nāfiʿ instead.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ﴿ ثمر ﴾ و ﴿ بثمره ﴾ بضم الثاء وسكون الميم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r6.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r6.claim: These readers use ḍamma on both thāʾ and mīm in ثمر and بثمره.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى ﴿ ثمر ﴾ و ﴿ بثمره ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r7.speaker: عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r7.claim: ʿĀṣim reads ثمر and بثمره with fatḥa on both thāʾ and mīm.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r7.anchor: وقرأ عاصم ﴿ ثمر ﴾ و ﴿ بثمره ﴾ بفتح الثاء والميم

QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#1/r1.claim: The standard thamar pattern means fruit or produce collectively.

QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#2/r1.claim: The thumur pattern is a plural of thamar and emphasizes multiple types of fruit.
QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#2/r1.anchor: Variant: ḍamma-ḍamma pattern (thumur) = plural of thamar, emphasizing multiplicity of fruit types

QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#3/r1.claim: The thumr pattern means wealth or property, moving the image from botanical produce to an economic register.
QIRAAT-ER:18:42:4#3/r1.anchor: Variant: ḍamma-sukūn (thumr) = wealth/property specifically (Lane's: thumr = māl, property)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#2/r1.claim: Qatada explains the garden's fruit as all its wealth, including fruit and other property.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وأحيط بثمره ﴾ قال الثمر من المال كله يعني الثمر وغيره من المال كله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وابن كثير ونافع وجماعة قراء المدينة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r9.claim: These readers pronounce thumar with ḍamma on both consonants, a plural of thimār.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وابن كثير ونافع وجماعة قراء المدينة: ثمر وبثمره بضم الثاء والميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r10.speaker: الأعمش وأبو رجاء وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r10.claim: These readers use a still mīm, either as a lightened form or as the plural of thamarah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r10.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وأبو رجاء وأبو عمرو بإسكان الميم فيهما تخفيفا أو جمع ثمرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر والحسن وجابر بن زيد والحجاج وعاصم وأبو حاتم ويعقوب عن رويس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r11.claim: This group reads both forms with fatḥa on thāʾ and mīm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر والحسن وجابر بن زيد والحجاج وعاصم وأبو حاتم ويعقوب عن رويس عنه بفتح الثاء والميم فيهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r12.speaker: رويس عن يعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r12.claim: Ruwais transmits ḍamma on both letters in thumar but fatḥa in bithamarihi for readers using the ḍamma form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p174/r12.anchor: قرأ رويس عن يعقوب ثمر بضمهما وبثمره بفتحهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r1.claim: The companion's refusal to associate anyone with God indirectly accuses the garden-owner of association, later made explicit in the owner's regret.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p179/r1.anchor: وفي قوله ولا أشرك بربي أحدا تعريض بإشراك صاحبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p180/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p180/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p180/r14.claim: God fulfilled the believer's hope by destroying the unbeliever's fruits; aḥīṭa bi-thamarihi extends from enemies surrounding someone to any comprehensive destruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p180/r14.anchor: فأخبر تعالى أنه أحيط بثمره وهو عبارة عن الإهلاك وأصله من أحاط به العدو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p180/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p180/r15.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p180/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the phrase a figurative expression for comprehensive punishment and ruin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p180/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: الإحاطة كناية عن عموم العذاب والفساد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r1.claim: The destruction apparently happened at night because he awoke to it, though aṣbaḥa can mean simply became and need not specify morning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r1.anchor: والظاهر أن الإحاطة كانت ليلا لقوله فأصبح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r2.claim: Turning his palms over means showing first their inner sides and then their backs, a gesture of regret for what he lost.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r2.anchor: ظاهره أنه يقلب كفيه ظهرا لبطن وهو أنه يبدي باطن كفه ثم يعوج كفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r3.claim: Other descriptions say he clapped one hand against the other or placed one palm against the back of the other.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r3.anchor: وقيل: يصفق بيده على الأخرى ويقلب كفيه ظهر البطن. وقيل:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r4.claim: Since the gesture signifies regret, the preposition phrase means he regretted the wealth spent building the garden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r4.anchor: ولما كان هذا الفعل كناية عن الندم عداه تعدية فعل الندم فقال على ما أنفق فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r5.claim: The phrase about the garden's collapsed trellises was discussed earlier in al-Baqara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r5.anchor: وهي خاوية على عروشها تقدم الكلام على هذه الجملة في أواخر البقرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r6.claim: The wish that he had not associated anyone with God apparently was voiced in this life as repentance after disaster, warning Quraysh and others against faith delayed until punishment arrives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r6.anchor: الظاهر أنه صدر منه ذلك في حالة الدنيا على جهة التوبة بعد حلول المصيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r7.claim: Some say God sent a fire that consumed the garden; the man then remembered his companion's advice and attributed the loss to his association and arrogance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r7.anchor: قيل: أرسل الله عليها نارا فأكلتها فتذكر موعظة أخيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r8.speaker: مفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r8.claim: Some commentators instead make the unbeliever's wish a statement in the Hereafter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p181/r8.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: هي حكاية عن قول الكافر هذه المقالة في الآخرة

FARRA:v2p145/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p145/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p145/r4.claim: خاوية على عروشها means fallen or empty upon its roofs.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268/r1.claim: Uḥīṭa bi-thamarihi means his crop was destroyed.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268/r2.claim: Turning one's hands means regret, a customary image for a regretful person.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268/r2.anchor: {فأصبح يقلب كفيه} أي نادما وهذا مما يوصف [به] النادم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p268/r3.claim: Khāwiya means ruined, and ʿurūsh are roofs.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r1.claim: أحيط بثمره means that the known wealth of both gardens and their contents was destroyed; surrounding enemies is extended metaphorically to total destruction.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r1.anchor: أهلك أمواله المعهودة من جنتيه وما فيهما وهو مأخوذ من إحاطة العدو

ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r2.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r2.claim: Al-Khafaji describes the image as a representative metaphor: the garden’s destruction resembles a people surrounded and annihilated by an enemy.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r2.anchor: شبه إهلاك جنتيه بما فيهما بإهلاك قوم حاط بهم عدو

ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r3.claim: The author says construing the image as metonymy is more apparent than the proposed kinds of metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r3.anchor: وجعل ذلك من باب الكناية أظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r4.claim: The clause coordinates with an omitted event, implied by context, before the destruction.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r5.claim: The author infers that destruction occurred at night from فأصبح; alternatively أصبح may mean simply “became.”

ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r6.claim: “Turning over his hands” may describe repeatedly exposing both palms and backs, or placing one palm over the other and reversing them.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r6.anchor: أن يبدي بطن كل منهما ثم يعوج يده حتى يبدو ظهر كل يفعل ذلك مرارا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r7.claim: The hand-turning is a metonym for regret and grief, unlike the idiom “turn the matter inside out,” which means shifting among topics.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r7.anchor: فهو كناية عن الندم والتحسر وليس ذلك من قوله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r8.claim: The phrase على ما أنفق links to the implied regret: he was grieving over what he spent.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p282#2/r8.anchor: فالجار والمجرور ظرف له متعلق بيقلب كأنه قيل فأصبح يندم على ما أنفق

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r1.claim: The prepositional phrase may instead be a settled circumstantial modifier meaning that he turns his hands while grieving; calling it emphatic depends on treating grief and regret as synonymous.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r1.anchor: أي متحسرا على ما أنفق وهو نظرا إلى المعنى الكنائي حال مؤكدة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r2.claim: Some distinguish grief as narrower than regret.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن التحسر الحزن وهو أخص

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r3.claim: A variant reads “his two hands are turned over”; on this reading, ما can be verbal (“his spending”) or relative (“what he spent”).

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r4.claim: He regrets the expenditure in particular because it could have been saved or used for other interests, and he had thought the garden indestructible.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r4.anchor: كان ما يمكن صيانته عن طوارق الحدثان وقد صرفه إلى مصالحها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r5.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r5.claim: Al-Khafaji says the garden and trees were abruptly annihilated by a heavenly calamity, as indicated by the immediate “then morning found him.”
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r5.anchor: إن الآية تدل على وقوع اتئصال نباتها وأشجارها عاجلا بآفة سماوية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r6.claim: خاوية means fallen or collapsed; the garden’s trellises are supports on which vines grow, and the collapse came down upon them.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r6.anchor: والعروش جمع عرش وهو هنا ما يصنع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r7.claim: Grapevines may be singled out because they are the main planting, their destruction entails the rest, or their cultivation cost the most.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r7.anchor: إما لأنها العمدة وهما من متمماتها وإما لأن الذكر هلاكها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r8.claim: The description makes a report that fire burned the orchard unlikely unless “garden” means the entire property and the phrase means general ruin.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r8.anchor: ثم هذه الجملة تبعد ما روي من أن الله تعالى أرسل عليها نارا فأحرقتها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r9.claim: ويقول coordinates with يقلب; some allow it as a circumstantial clause with an implicit pronoun, despite the rarity of an affirmative present verb with circumstantial و.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283/r9.anchor: عطف على ( يقلب ) وجوز أبو البقاء وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r1.claim: The garden-owner remembers his brother’s admonition and recognizes that his associating partners with God brought the loss.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r1.anchor: كأنه تذكر موعظة أخيه وعلم أنه إنما أتى من قبل شركه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r2.claim: One possibility is that his words constitute repentance and renewed faith, since regret over past shirk suggests he now believes.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون توبة من الشرك وندما عليه فيكون تجديدا للايمان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r3.claim: The author rejects that repentance: regret at disbelief alone is not faith, and here he regrets losing his garden rather than shirk as sin; later context still shows denial of resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r3.anchor: لم يتحقق هنا من الكافر ندم عليه من حيث هو كفر بل بسبب هلاك جنتيه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r4.claim: Repentance for sin requires resolving not to return and regretting the act as sinful, as discussed in al-Mawaqif.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r4.anchor: إذا عزم على أن لا يعود وكان الندم عليها من حيث كونها معصية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r5.claim: If the statement is instead spoken on Judgment Day, as some exegetes say, renewed faith there is unanimously useless.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p283#2/r5.anchor: إذا قيل إن هذا حكاية لما يقوله الكافر يوم القيامة كما ذهب إليه بعض المفسرين

MAJAZ:v1p404/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p404/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p404/r1.claim: Turning one's palms means becoming regretful and grieving over what was spent and lost.
MAJAZ:v1p404/r1.anchor: «فأصبح يقلب كفيه على ما أنفق فيها» (42) أي فأصبح نادما، والعرب تقول ذلك للنادم

MAJAZ:v1p404/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p404/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p404/r2.claim: Khāwiyah ʿalā ʿurūshihā means empty on its houses.
MAJAZ:v1p404/r2.anchor: «وهي خاوية على عروشها» (42) مجازه: خالية على بيوتها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p173#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p173#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p173#2/r3.claim: God's punishment surrounded the garden's fruit, sent fire to destroy it, and made its water disappear.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p173#2/r3.anchor: {وأحيط بثمره} أي: أحاط العذاب بثمر جنته وذلك أن الله تعالى أرسل عليها نارا فأهلكتها وغار ماؤها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p173#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p173#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p173#2/r4.claim: The owner flips his hands in regret over what he spent; the garden lies fallen on its supports, and he regrets having associated anyone with God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p173#2/r4.anchor: {فأصبح} صاحبها الكافر {يقلب كفيه} أي: يصفق بيده على الأخرى ويقلب كفيه ظهرا لبطن تأسفا وتلهفا

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r1.claim: Being encompassed means his property was ruined; the expression comes from an enemy surrounding and overpowering someone, as with the idiom for destroying something.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r1.anchor: وهو مأخوذ من أحاط به العدو فإنه إذا أحاط به غلبه

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r2.claim: Turning the palms over and over expresses regret; the phrase syntactically means he regretted what he spent on the garden.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r2.anchor: فأصبح يقلب كفيه } ظهرا لبطن تلهفا وتحسرا

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r3.claim: The garden lies fallen on its trellises, with vines collapsed above them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r3.anchor: بأن سقطت عروشها على الأرض وسقطت الكروم فوقها عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r4.claim: The owner recalls his brother's warning and thinks his association caused the loss; his lament may be repentance and remorse for prior shirk.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:42/r4.anchor: كأنه تذكر موعظة أخيه وعلم أنه أتى من قبل شركه

NAHHAS:v2p458/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p458/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p458/r2.claim: In ‘his produce was surrounded,’ the passive has an implicit verbal noun as its subject; the genitive form may function in the nominative, while ‘he began turning’ is a circumstantial accusative.
NAHHAS:v2p458/r2.anchor: اسم ما لم يسم فاعله مضمر وهو المصدر ، ويجوز أن يكون المخفوض في موضع رفع ^ ( فأصبح يقلب ) ^ في موضع نصب أي منقلبا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r1.claim: The garden’s entire produce was destroyed; the passive construction emphasizes the comprehensive ruin without naming a particular agent and suggests its ease.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r1.anchor: بني للمفعول لأن الفكر حاصل بإحاطة الهلاك من غير نظر إلى فاعل مخصوص

BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r2.claim: The owner turns his hands in regret, striking one against the other over what he spent cultivating and improving the garden.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r3.claim: The garden lies empty and collapsed: its supports fell, then the structure they carried fell over them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r3.anchor: وهي خاوية } أي ساقطة مع الخلو { على عروشها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r4.claim: His wish not to have associated anyone with God is regret over worldly loss, not concern for faith or salvation; his understanding remains bound to visible things.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p470/r4.anchor: لقصور عقله ووقوفه مع المحسوسات المشاهدات

DURR-FULL:v5p394/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r3.claim: Qatada says the owner's turning his palms describes clapping in grief over what he spent and lost.
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r3.anchor: {وأحيط بثمره فأصبح يقلب كفيه} قال يصفق {على ما أنفق فيها} متلهفا على ما فاته

DURR-FULL:v5p394/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the slippery ground is smooth and barren; both gardens were destroyed, the owner turned his hands in regret, and the trellises were overturned.
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r4.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله: {صعيدا زلقا} قال: الصعيد الأملس والزلق التي ليس فيها نبات

DURR-FULL:v5p394/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says God's decree encompassed the garden's fruit and destroyed it.
DURR-FULL:v5p394/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {وأحيط بثمره} قال: أحاط به أمر الله فهلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r8.claim: The calamity's encompassing the garden is a figure for the totality of its destruction and ruin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r8.anchor: هذا خبر من الله عن إحاطة العذاب بحال هذا المثل به، وقد تقدم القول في الثمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r9.claim: Turning the palms means placing one palm against the back of the other, the gesture of regret; glossing it as clapping is inaccurate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r9.anchor: يريد يضع بطن إحداهما على ظهر الأخرى، وذلك فعل المتلهف المتأسف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r10.claim: The trellises or roofs fell first, then the walls collapsed over them, leaving the garden hollow and ruined.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r10.anchor: يريد أن السقوف وقعت، وهي العروش، ثم تهدمت الحيطان عليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r11.claim: Some commentators place the man's wish not to associate a partner with God in the afterlife; Ibn Atiyya allows that he said it in worldly repentance after the calamity as a warning to Quraysh and others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p518#2/r11.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين: هي حكاية عن قول الكافر هذه المقالة في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r1.claim: God's punishment encompassed the garden's produce; turning his palms means striking one hand against the other in regret at what he spent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى وأحيط بثمره أي أحاط الله العذاب بثمره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r2.claim: Here في means على; خاوية means empty and fallen over its trellises, with the walls standing and roofs collapsed inside.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r2.anchor: وفي هاهنا بمعنى على وهي خاوية أي خالية ساقطة على عروشها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r3.claim: After God removed his blessing and fulfilled his brother's warning, the man regretted associating partners with God, when regret could no longer help him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r3.anchor: فأخبر الله تعالى أنه لما سلبه ما انعم به عليه وحقق ما أنذره به أخوه في الدنيا ندم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r4.claim: Another view is that he will say this only at the Resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p146/r4.anchor: وقيل إنما يقول هذا في القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r1.claim: The orchard owner's fruits, or his wealth by another interpretation, were surrounded by ruin: the disaster the believer had warned about struck the garden that had distracted him from God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r1.anchor: بأمواله، أو بثماره على القول الآخر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r2.claim: Qatada explains turning the hands as clapping them in grief and regret for the wealth he had spent and lost.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: يصفق كفيه متأسفا متلهفا على الأموال التي أذهبها عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r3.claim: His clan or children, whom he had boasted in, could not support him; he could not save himself, and at that moment true authority belonged to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p160/r3.anchor: أي: عشيرة أو ولد، كما افتخر بهم واستعز

JISHUMI:v6p4423/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r2.claim: The destruction of the man's wealth is punishment and a benefit because it makes him regret what he did.
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r2.anchor: ما أحاط بماله كان عقوبة له ومصلحة، حيث له ندم على ما تقدم عنه

JISHUMI:v6p4423/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r3.claim: If losing wealth causes such regret, the regret of one who loses himself to eternal punishment is greater still.
JISHUMI:v6p4423/r3.anchor: فلأن تعظم حسرة من خسر نفسه وأوبقها بعذاب الأبد أولى

SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r1.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r1.claim: A reading has تقلب كفاه, meaning his two palms turn over.
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r1.anchor: قرئ " تقلب كفاه " ، أي: تتقلب كفاه.

SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r2.claim: أصبح may retain its morning sense or mean became; turning the hands is a metonym for remorse.
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r2.anchor: " أصبح ": يجوز أن تكون على بابها،

SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r3.claim: على ما أنفق attaches to يقلب with على licensed by the implied sense of regretting.
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق ب " يقلب " ، وإنما عدي

SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r4.claim: فيها may attach to an omitted phrase and describe the subject of يقلب as regretful; the author says this is semantic paraphrase, while the formal parse is an unrestricted state.
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r5.claim: ويقول may coordinate with يقلب or function as a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:18:42/r5.anchor: يجوز أن يكون معطوفا على " يقلب "

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r1.claim: The garden's produce was destroyed, fulfilling the brother's warning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r1.anchor: وهذا أول ما حقق الله به إنذار أخيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r2.claim: Turning his palms expresses regret for spending and grief at the loss.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r2.anchor: يقلب كفيه ندما على ما أنفق فيها وأسفا على ما تلف

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r3.claim: Alternatively, he searches his estate for compensation; hand can mean property.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r3.anchor: لأن الملك قد يعبر عنه باليد , من قولهم في يده مال

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r4.claim: The garden lay overturned; both its foundation and produce perished as a calamity answering transgression.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p308/r4.anchor: منقلبة على عاليها فجمع عليه بين هلاك الأصل والثمر

MUJAHID:v1p376#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p376#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p376#4/r1.claim: Mujahid says the ruined garden's fruit also means gold and silver.
MUJAHID:v1p376#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وأحيط بثمره ﴾ يعني ذهبا وفضة أيضا

MUQATIL:18:42-44/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:42-44/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:42-44/r1.claim: The garden's destruction makes its owner slap his hands in regret for what he spent; the garden's trellises have fallen.
MUQATIL:18:42-44/r1.anchor: { فأصبح يقلب كفيه } ، يعني يصفق بكفيه ندامة، { على ما أنفق فيها وهي خاوية على عروشها } ،

MUQATIL:18:42-44/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:42-44/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:42-44/r2.claim: The owner regrets having associated anyone with his Lord.
MUQATIL:18:42-44/r2.anchor: ويقول يليتني لم أشرك بربي أحدا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r1.claim: “He was surrounded in its fruit” is a metaphor for its destruction, first used of an enemy surrounding and controlling someone.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r1.anchor: هو عبارة عن أهلاكه واصله من أحاط به العدو لأنه إذا أحاط به

NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r2.claim: The garden's owner is the unbeliever; turning his palms over one another is a conventional image of remorse and grief.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r2.anchor: يضرب احداهما على الأخرى ندما وتحسرا وإنما صار تقليب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r3.claim: The vines' trellises collapsed onto the ground and the vines fell over them; “on what he spent in it” means its cultivation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r3.anchor: يعني أن كرومها المعرشة سقطت عروشها عل الأرض وسقطت فوقها الكروم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r4.claim: Remembering his brother's warning, he recognized that disbelief and transgression had caused the loss; his wish came too late to help.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r4.anchor: تذكر موعظة أخيه فعلم أنه أتى من جهة كفره وطغيانه فتمنى لو لم يكن مشركا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r5.claim: The final wish may also be read as repentance from polytheism, regret for his past, and entry into faith.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p15#3/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون توبة من الشرك وندما على ما كان منه ودخولا في الإيمان

QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r1.claim: Aḥīṭa bi-thamarihi has an implicit verbal noun as its grammatical subject, though the genitive form may also be construed as nominative; the whole fortune was destroyed, fulfilling the companion’s warning.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r1.anchor: اسم ما لم يسم فاعله مضمر، وهو المصدر

QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r2.claim: He turns his hands over in regret; alternatively, he turns over his dominion and sees nothing left to compensate what he spent, since hand can mean ownership.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r2.anchor: أي فأصبح الكافر يضرب إحدى يديه على الأخرى ندما

QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r3.claim: Asbaḥa indicates the destruction happened at night, as in the story of the garden visited while its owners slept and left blackened by morning.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r3.anchor: على أن هذا الإهلاك جرى بالليل

QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r4.claim: Khāwiyat ʿalā ʿurūshihā describes it as empty and fallen upon its roofs; the root can describe stars setting, barren land, or a collapsed house.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r4.anchor: أي خالية قد سقط بعضها على بعض مأخوذ من خوت النجوم تخوى خيا أمحلت

QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r5.claim: The garden fell onto its trellises, destroying both crop and structure; this great calamity answers his transgression.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r5.anchor: فجمع عليه بين هلاك الثمر والأصل، وهذا من أعظم الجوائح، مقابلة على بغيه

QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r6.claim: He wishes he had not associated anyone with his Lord, now recognizing that his blessings came from God’s power; the regret comes too late.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:42/r6.anchor: أي يا ليتني عرفت نعم الله علي، وعرفت أنها كانت بقدرة الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p289/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p289/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p289/r3.claim: God's punishment encompassed the produce; the walls remained without roofs after the roofs fell to the ground.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r19.claim: The fruit being surrounded is a metaphor for its total destruction, extended from an enemy encircling and taking control.
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r19.anchor: وهو عبارة عن إهلاكه بالكلية وأصله من إحاطة العدو

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r20.claim: The same idiom appears in the account of Jacob requiring his sons to be surrounded, meaning besieged by an enemy.
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r20.anchor: ومنه قوله : { إلا أن يحاط بكم }

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r21.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r21.claim: Turning his palms is a metaphor for regret and grief: a deeply sorrowful person claps or rubs one hand against the other over his lost investment.
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r21.anchor: وهو كناية عن الندم والحسرة فإن من عظمت حسرته

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r22.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r22.claim: The collapsed trellises may be grape arbors beneath which the walls fell, or roofs that fell onto the walls; either way the phrase means complete ruin.
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r22.anchor: أي ساقطة على عروشها فيمكن أن يكون المراد بالعروش

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r23.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r23.claim: The ruined man recalls the believer's declaration of God's oneness and regrets having associated a partner with his Lord.

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r24.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r24.claim: The ruin does not prove that believers are spared affliction: most trials also befall believers, and a prophetic report says prophets, saints, then the best are most tested.
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r24.anchor: خص البلاء بالأنبياء ثم الأولياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r25.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r25.claim: His regret does not establish sincere repentance: he wanted monotheism only because he thought it would preserve his garden, so God did not accept it.
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r25.anchor: إنما ندم على الشرك لاعتقاده أنه لو كان موحدا غير مشرك لبقيت عليه جنته

RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r26.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r26.claim: His grief is severe because he spent his life seeking worldly gain and neglecting religion; now both his worldly gain and religious opportunity are lost.
RAZI-FULL:v21p108#2/r26.anchor: لأجل أنه أنفق عمره في تحصيل الدنيا وكان معرضا في كل عمره عن طلب الدين

STUDYQURAN:18:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r1.claim: “His fruit was encompassed” can mean he lost all his wealth.
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r1.anchor: His fruit was encompassed—that is, by ruin—meaning either that he lost all his wealth

STUDYQURAN:18:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r2.claim: Alternatively, his garden was unexpectedly destroyed as his believing brother had warned.
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r2.anchor: or that his garden was destroyed unexpectedly as his believing brother had warned him in vv. 40–41

STUDYQURAN:18:42/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r3.claim: Wringing his hands expresses remorse and regret.
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r3.anchor: Upon seeing this he began to wring his hands as a gesture of remorse and regret

STUDYQURAN:18:42/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r4.claim: Despite his earlier boast of having more men, the ruined disbeliever has no party to help him apart from God and cannot help himself.
STUDYQURAN:18:42/r4.anchor: Despite the disbeliever’s earlier boasts that he was stronger in men than his brother (v. 34)

TAB-FULL:v15p268/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r1.claim: A calamity destroyed the garden’s crops and fruit, which the owner once thought could never perish; he turned his hands over in grief at his lost investment.
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r1.anchor: يقلب كفيه ظهرا لبطن، تلهفا وأسفا على ذهاب نفقته

TAB-FULL:v15p268/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r2.claim: Qatāda explains turning the hands as clapping them in regret.
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {فأصبح يقلب كفيه} [الكهف: 42] أي يصفق

TAB-FULL:v15p268/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r3.claim: The garden is empty and collapsed over its supports; the owner wishes he had not associated anyone with God.

TAB-FULL:v15p268/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r4.claim: After his possessions disappear and he is left alone with his deeds, the unbeliever regrets having disbelieved or associated anything with God.
TAB-FULL:v15p268/r4.anchor: إذا هلك وزالت عنه دنياه وانفرد بعمله، ود أنه لم يكن كفر بالله

TABATABAI:18:42-44/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r3.claim: “He was encompassed by its fruit” figuratively means total ruin, like an enemy encircling someone and cutting off every helper; the Qurʾān uses the expression in 10:22.

TABATABAI:18:42-44/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r4.claim: Turning the palms is a gesture of regret; the garden lying collapsed on its trellises depicts complete destruction, whether the root is understood as falling or emptiness.
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r4.anchor: كناية عن الندامة فإن النادم كثيرا ما يقلب كفيه ظهرا لبطن

TABATABAI:18:42-44/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r5.claim: His wish not to have associated anyone with God means he regrets relying on his garden, self, and worldly causes as though they had independent effects.
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r5.anchor: ولم أسكن إلى ما سكنت إليه واغتررت به من نفسي وسائر الأسباب

TABATABAI:18:42-44/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r6.claim: The companion’s words verbally correct the man’s claims, while the garden’s ruin demonstrates the error in expecting worldly permanence, trusting wealth and followers, and claiming self-sufficiency.
TABATABAI:18:42-44/r6.anchor: بيانا قوليا لخطأ الرجل في كفره وشركه

TABRISI:18:39-42/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:39-42/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:39-42/r6.claim: The garden's destruction means its trees and palms were ruined completely; the report says God sent fire and the water disappeared.
TABRISI:18:39-42/r6.anchor: أهلك وأحيط العذاب بأشجاره ونخيله فهلكت عن آخرها

TABRISI:18:39-42/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:39-42/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:39-42/r7.claim: Turning the palms over each other expresses grief and regret; Ibn Abbas explains it as striking one hand against the other over the money spent.
TABRISI:18:39-42/r7.anchor: وهو أن يضرب يديه واحدة على الأخرى عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:18:39-42/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:39-42/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:39-42/r8.claim: The garden lying fallen on its trellises means its roof collapsed first and its walls then fell over it; another gloss takes the structures as empty houses with trees gone.
TABRISI:18:39-42/r8.anchor: وذلك أن السقف ينهدم أولا ثم ينهدم الحائط على السقف

TABRISI:18:39-42/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:39-42/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:39-42/r9.claim: One view says the owner regretted his associationism only because his wealth vanished and gained nothing; another says he truly repented of shirk and believed.
TABRISI:18:39-42/r9.anchor: إنه ندم على ما كان منه من الشرك بالله تعالى وآمن

THALABI:v6p171/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p171/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p171/r16.claim: Destruction surrounded the fruit of both gardens; ثمره covers every kind of fruit.
THALABI:v6p171/r16.anchor: أي أحاط الهلاك بثمر جنتيه، وهي جميع صنوف الثمار

THALABI:v6p171/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p171/r17.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p171/r17.claim: He interprets ثمره as gold and silver.

THALABI:v6p171/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p171/r18.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p171/r18.claim: God sent fire against the gardens, destroying them, and their water sank away.
THALABI:v6p171/r18.anchor: وذلك أن الله أرسل عليها نارا فأهلكها وغار ماؤها

THALABI:v6p171/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p171/r19.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p171/r19.claim: The ruined owner turns his hands over one another in regret and grief.
THALABI:v6p171/r19.anchor: يصفق يده على الأخرى، وتقليب كفيه ظهرا لبطن تأسفا وتلهفا

THALABI:v6p171/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p171/r20.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p171/r20.claim: In أنفقت فيها, فيها means عليها, as في does in the cited wording about crucifying on palm trunks.
THALABI:v6p171/r20.anchor: يعني: عليها كقوله: ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل

THALABI:v6p171/r21.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p171/r21.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p171/r21.claim: The garden is collapsed over its roofs and empty of its plantings and buildings.
THALABI:v6p171/r21.anchor: ساقطة على سقوفها، خالية من غرسها وبنائها

THALABI:v6p171/r22.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p171/r22.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p171/r22.claim: The owner wishes he had not associated anyone with his Lord.
THALABI:v6p171/r22.anchor: ويقول يا ليتني لم أشرك بربي أحدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r1.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r1.claim: The common vocalization distinguishes thamar, meaning wealth, from thumur, meaning edible fruit; most exegetes take it as wealth here, while Ibn Zayd says it means the fruit-bearing trees themselves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r1.anchor: فلأن أهل اللغة فرقوا بين الثمر والثمر # فقالوا: الثمر المال، والثمر المأكول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r2.claim: The common reading is stronger because the owner turns his hands over what he spent on the garden, and spending usually goes to the productive trees and assets.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r2.anchor: وهذه القراءة أقوى الوجوه لقوله: {فأصبح يقلب كفيه على ما أنفق فيها}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq prefers thamar because the earlier statement that both gardens yielded produce already establishes that meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r3.anchor: الثمر هاهنا أحسن؛ لأن قوله: {كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها} قد دل على الثمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r4.claim: Abu Amr says both vocalized forms can denote kinds of wealth; the word here covers the garden, property, palms, and trees.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r4.anchor: وحكي عن أبي عمرو أنه قال: (الثمر والثمر أنواع المال) (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r5.claim: Both readings can be clearer if they denote wealth and all the garden's assets; the reading in Asim's earlier clause as a particular crop is weak because that fruit was already implied, while the broad reading covers produce and roots.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r5.anchor: فمن قرأ: بثمره وثمره كان قوله أبين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r6.speaker: سلام أبو المنذر عن محمد بن سلام
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r6.claim: Salam says one reading means all wealth and the other a plural of fruit; Yunus regards them as equivalent, but al-Wahidi rejects that conflation and preserves the distinction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p11/r6.anchor: وقال محمد بن سلام: (قال سلام أبو المنذر القارئ (¬1): من قرأ: "ثمر" قال: من كل المال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r1.claim: “Its fruits were surrounded” means the punishment destroyed them, like an army encircling and wiping out an enemy.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r2.claim: “Its fruits” refers to the fruit trees and date palms.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r3.claim: Turning the two palms means striking one hand against the other in regret.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r3.anchor: يضرب يديه واحدة على الأخرى ندامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi describes the gesture as clapping one hand against the other in regret.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (يصفق بالواحدة على # الأخرى ندما)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج والمفضل وابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r5.claim: The phrase is an idiom for regret over what was lost: people turn their hands or palms as they reconsider a loss, much like biting one's hand; a poetic line illustrates the gesture.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p27/r5.anchor: يقال: فلان يقلب كفيه على ما فاته، وتقليب الكفين يفعله النادم كثيرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r1.claim: Arabic can say one spent money “in” a house or garment, or “on” it; here “in” may mean “on,” as in the verse about crucifying people on palm trunks.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r1.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون هاهنا بمعنى: على، كقوله: {ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r2.claim: The collapsed trellises include building roofs and vine frameworks: the structures lie fallen and empty of their trellised growth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r2.anchor: والعروش في هذه الآية تعم سقوف الأبنية، وما عرش للكروم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r3.claim: The owner wishes he had not associated anyone with God, but the wish comes too late; God stripped his worldly blessings and his regret can no longer help.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p28/r3.anchor: تمنى منه حين لا ينفعه التمني. أخبر الله تعالى أنه سلبه ما أنعم عليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:42-44/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:42-44/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:42-44/r1.claim: The fruitful trees were destroyed, leaving the garden collapsed on its trellises; the owner turned his hands over in regret and wished he had not associated anyone with God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:42-44/r1.anchor: يضرب يديه واحدة على الأخرى ندامة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r7.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r7.claim: The garden was surrounded by destruction overnight; by morning its owner wrung or struck his hands in regret over what he had spent, lamenting his loss.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r7.anchor: } يقلب كفيه { [الكهف: 42] يسفق كفيه في تفسير الحسن وقتادة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r8.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r8.claim: Qatāda interprets the owner's hand-wringing as grief over what he lost; Ibn Mujāhid's father says the destroyed fruit means wealth of gold and silver.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r8.anchor: وقال ابن مجاهد، عن أبيه:} وأحيط بثمره { [الكهف: 42] مثل قوله:} وكان له ثمر { [الكهف: 34] : ذهب وفضة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r9.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says the garden is empty over its trellises, with the soil remaining after its plants vanished.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p186/r9.anchor: قال:} وهي خاوية على عروشها { [الكهف: 42] قال الحسن: عروشها: التراب، قد ذهب ما فيها من النبات.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r1.claim: Another view says the garden was overturned onto its roofs.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r2.claim: The owner speaks in the Hereafter, wishing in this life that he had not associated anyone with God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p188/r2.anchor: ويقول { [الكهف: 42] في الآخرة. } يا ليتني لم أشرك بربي { [الكهف: 42] في الدنيا. أحدا.

ELMALILI:18:32-44/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:32-44/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:32-44/r2.claim: After his wealth was overtaken and the garden collapsed over its trellises, the man wrung his hands over his expenses and wished he had not associated anyone with God.
ELMALILI:18:32-44/r2.anchor: bütün serveti istîlâ ediliverdi, bunun üzerine ona yaptığı masraflara karşı avuçlarını oğuşturdu kaldı

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The orchard is destroyed by a sudden calamity; its fences collapse and the owner wakes to the ruin he had thought impossible.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Finally, the orchard reached the same fate with which the believer had warned his companion. An earthly or heavenly calamity decimated it in the blink of an eye.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: His wish not to associate partners means he regrets arrogance that treated the orchard as his own achievement and entitlement; he should have seen it as God’s gift and been grateful.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: it was a gift of God and he should have been greateful for it.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.speaker: النيسابوري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.claim: Al-Nīsābūrī reads the gardens as desire and world, fruit as cravings, boasting of wealth and status as inclination and blameworthy traits, expecting a better garden as delusion about God, and turning hands over as regret for wasted life and good potential.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p309#2/r5.anchor: قال ذلك غرورا بالله تعالى وكرمه

QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.claim: Outwardly, one of two garden owners thanked his Creator while the other disbelieved his Provider; the latter's garden was ruined and he regretted neglecting gratitude.
QUSHAYRI:v2p220/r2.anchor: فشكر أحدهما لخالقه وكفر الآخر برازقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p327/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p327/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p327/r1.claim: The present-tense account of his saying conveys repeated regret after punishment, when regret can no longer help.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p327/r1.anchor: وجملة ويقول } حكاية لتندمه على ما فرط منه حين لا ينفعه الندم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p327/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p327/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p327/r2.claim: The vocative signals anguish; laytani personifies the wish as something called to appear, and the lament implies that he now believes in God alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p327/r2.anchor: وهذا ندم على الإشراك فيما مضى وهو يؤذن بأنه آمن بالله وحده حينئذ

JISHUMI:v6p4420/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r5.claim: Under passive أحيط, ثمره is nominative as the grammatical subject.
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r5.anchor: (ثمره) موضعه الضم ب (أحيط) لأنه اسم ما لم يسم فاعله،

JISHUMI:v6p4420/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r7.claim: The garden’s produce was destroyed; this may mean all its fruits or all the owner’s wealth.
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r7.anchor: وأحيط بثمره أي: أحاط الهلاك بثماره أي: أدار به فأهلكه حتى لم يخرج منه شيء، قيل بثمره بجميع، ثمار جنته، وقيل: بجميع أمواله،

JISHUMI:v6p4420/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r8.claim: A report says God sent fire on the garden, destroyed it, and drained its water.
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r8.anchor: وفي الخبر: أنه تعالى أرسل عليها نارا فأهلكها وغار ماؤها،

JISHUMI:v6p4420/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r9.claim: The owner turns his hands in regret over the large amount he spent.
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r9.anchor: فأصبح يعني الكافر يقلب كفيه يصفق بإحدى يديه على الأخرى ويقلبها ظهرا لبطن

JISHUMI:v6p4420/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r10.claim: The collapsed garden is described as roofless and dry, upside down, or with walls standing but no roofs, according to al-Asamm.
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r10.anchor: وقيل: صار أعلاها أسفلها، وقيل: حيطانها قائمة ليس لها سقوف

JISHUMI:v6p4420/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r11.claim: Its trees and structures vanished, leaving useless walls.
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r11.anchor: فذهب شجرها وأبنيتها وبقيت جدرانا لا خير فيها

JISHUMI:v6p4420/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r12.claim: His wish not to have associated partners was driven by desire to preserve wealth and would not benefit him; sincere repentance would have helped.
JISHUMI:v6p4420/r12.anchor: فتمنى الإيمان لبقاء ماله لا لوجوبه وكان لا ينفعه، ولو ندم على الكفر وآمن بالله تحقيقا لانتفع به،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r1.claim: ‘Was encompassed’ signifies that the garden was destroyed; the image comes from an enemy surrounding and mastering someone, then extends to any destruction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r1.anchor: به عبارة عن إهلاكه . وأصله من أحاط به العدو ؛ لأنه إذا أحاط به فقد ملكه واستولى عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r2.claim: Turning the palms over is a metaphor for regret and grief, as a regretful person turns the hands palm up and down; the wording uses ‘over’ because regret takes that construction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r2.anchor: كناية عن الندم والتحسر ، لأن النادم يقلب كفيه ظهرا لبطن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r3.claim: The regret concerns what he spent building the garden.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r3.anchor: فأصبح يندم { على ما أنفق فيها } أي أنفق في عمارتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r4.claim: The trellises of its vines fell to the ground, with the vines falling over them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r4.anchor: يعني أن كرومها المعرشة سقطت عروشها على الأرض ، وسقطت فوقها الكروم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r5.claim: One reported explanation says God sent fire that consumed the garden.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r5.anchor: قيل : أرسل الله عليها نارا فأكلتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r6.claim: Remembering his brother’s admonition, the owner realizes his associationism and rebellion brought the disaster and wishes he had not associated anything with God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r6.anchor: تذكر موعظة أخيه فعلم أنه أتى من جهة شركه وطغيانه ، فتمنى لو لم يكن مشركا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r7.claim: The wish may also be repentance for associationism, regret for his conduct, and entry into faith.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p676/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون توبة من الشرك ، وندما على ما كان منه ، ودخولا في الإيمان

IBNMUJAHID:v1p402/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p402/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p402/r1.claim: Of 37 additional yāʾs in the sura, nine differ: Nāfiʿ opens all listed forms except the three maʿī ṣabran; Abū ʿAmr quiesces that trio and satجدني; Ibn Kathīr follows him except min dūnī awliyāʾ; Ḥafṣ opens the trio.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p402/r1.anchor: فى هذه السورة سبع وثلاثون ياء إضافة اختلفوا فى تسع منها قوله ﴿ ربي أعلم ﴾

BURHAN:v2p213/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p213/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p213/r1.claim: The ruined owner turns his hands over in regret.
BURHAN:v2p213/r1.anchor: وكذا ﴿ فأصبح يقلب كفيه ﴾ أي نادما

BURHAN:v2p213/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p213/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p213/r9.claim: The Qur'an's wording may be explicit with only one meaning or apparent while permitting others; verbal and contextual clues resolve ambiguity, with attached verbal clues either redirecting a word or clarifying it.
BURHAN:v2p213/r9.anchor: اعلم ان الكتاب هو القرآن المتلو وهو إما نص

ITQAN:v3p49/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p49/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p49/r11.claim: Less familiar usages mean listening, being arrogant, and being regretful, respectively.
ITQAN:v3p49/r11.anchor: ومنها عدم كثرة الاستعمال الآن نحو ﴿ يلقون السمع ﴾ أي يسمعون ﴿ ثاني عطفه ﴾ أي متكبرا ﴿ فأصبح يقلب كفيه ﴾ أي نادما

DAMGHANI:v1p462/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p462/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p462/r15.claim: Infāq can mean spending on construction or cultivation, as in the ruined garden.
DAMGHANI:v1p462/r15.anchor: النفقة العمارة قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r1.claim: Iḥāṭa is surrounding something on every side; a garden is called a ḥāʾiṭ because it encloses many fruits.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r1.anchor: الإحاطة : الاستدارة بالشيء من جميع جوانبه . ويقال للبستان : الحائط ، لأنه يجمع كثيرا من الثمار

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains the garden’s name as referring to its surrounding, benefiting, and protecting its owner.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري : لأنه يحوط صاحبه وينفعه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r5.claim: A third sense is destruction, illustrated by the ruined garden and the sin that overtakes its bearer.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p114/r5.anchor: والثالث : الإهلاك . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r1.claim: Fī is fundamentally a preposition of location, though context can license its metaphorical use.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r1.anchor: حرف موضوع في الأصل للظرفية . تقول . زيد في الدار

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r2.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r2.claim: Abū Zakariyyā calls expressions such as being in knowledge or work metaphorical; possession is pictured as something in one’s hand through strong control.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r2.anchor: قال أبو زكريا : وقولهم : زيد في العلم . وعمرو في الشغل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r5.claim: The third use means ʿalā, as in spending upon the garden and crucifying upon palm trunks.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r5.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى ' على ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف :

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r4.claim: Being surrounded means approaching destruction, as an encircled enemy or town nears ruin; the same image describes the garden's lost fruit.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p106/r4.anchor: أي دنوا من الهلاك. وأصل هذا

NASHR:v1p280/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p280/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p280/r1.claim: In idghām kabīr the two letters remain articulated for lightening rather than one literally entering the other, contrary to some; only manāsikakum and mā salakakum are assimilated within one word.
NASHR:v1p280/r1.anchor: وليس بإدخال حرف بحرف كما ذهب إليه بعضهم، بل الصحيح أن الحرفين ملفوظ بهما كما وصفنا طلبا للتخفيف

NASHR:v1p280/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p280/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p280/r2.claim: Alif and hamza neither assimilate nor receive assimilation; five letters meet none of their like, kind, or neighbors, six meet only identicals, five meet only kind or nearby letters, and eleven meet all; the totals are 17 and 16.
NASHR:v1p280/r2.anchor: فجملة اللاقي مثله متحركا سبعة عشر، وجملة اللاقي مجانسه أو مقاربه ستة عشر حرفا

NASHR:v1p280/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p280/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p280/r3.claim: Bāʾ examples include la-dhahaba bi-samʿihim and al-kitāb bi-l-ḥaqq; the total is 57, or 59 for readers who do not join the sūra ending to the basmala.
NASHR:v1p280/r3.anchor: سبعة وخمسون حرفا عند من يبسمل بين السورتين

NASHR:v1p280/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p280/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p280/r4.claim: The listed tāʾ cases total fourteen, including word-final tāʾs that become hāʾ when pausing.

NASHR:v1p280/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p280/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p280/r5.claim: Thāʾ has three examples; ḥāʾ has two, including al-nikāḥ ḥattā and wa-lā abraḥu ḥattā in al-Kahf.
NASHR:v1p280/r5.anchor: وهو ثلاثة أحرف: حيث ثقفتموهم في البقرة والنساء

NASHR:v1p280/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p280/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p280/r6.anchor: نحو شهر رمضان، الأبرار ربنا وجملته خمس وثلاثون حرفا

NASHR:v1p280/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p280/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p280/r7.claim: Sīn examples are al-nāsu sukārā and li-l-nāsi sawāʾ in al-Ḥajj and al-shamsu sirājan in Nūḥ, three in all.
NASHR:v1p280/r7.anchor: الناس سكارى، للناس سواء كلاهما في الحج الشمس سراجا في نوح ثلاثة مواضع لا غير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r1.claim: Tafsir began in the Prophet’s lifetime, when companions asked about Quranic meanings; later leading interpreters included Ali, Ibn Abbas, Zayd, Ubayy, Ibn Masud, and Abdullah ibn Amr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r1.anchor: قد سأل عن بعض معاني القرآن كما سأله عمر رضي الله عنه عن الكلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r2.claim: Tafsir spread as non-Arab converts needed the Quran explained, and Ibn Ashur regards it as the noblest and foremost Islamic science.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r2.anchor: حين دخل في الإسلام من لم يكن عربي السجية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj of Mecca (80–149 AH) was the first to compile tafsir, covering many verses and gathering reports, especially from Ibn Abbas’s students Ata and Mujahid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r3.anchor: أول من صنف فيه عبد الملك بن جريج المكي المولود سنة 80 ه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r4.claim: The tafsir of Ibn Abbas transmitted through Muhammad al-Kalbi from Abu Salih was criticized; Abu Salih was accused of lying, making this one of the weakest transmissions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r4.anchor: وقد رمي أبو صالح بالكذب حتى لقب بكلمة دروغدت بالفارسية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r5.claim: Adding Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Suddi’s route through al-Kalbi was called a chain of lies, contrasted with the so-called golden chain of Malik, Nafi, and Ibn Umar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r5.anchor: فإذا انضم إليها رواية محمد بن مروان السدى عن الكلبي فهي سلسلة الكذب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r6.claim: It was alleged that al-Kalbi was associated with Abdullah ibn Saba, who promoted extreme claims about Ali, including that Ali had not died and would return.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r6.anchor: الكلبي كان من أصحاب عبد الله بن سبأ اليهودي الأصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r7.claim: Among reports attributed to Ibn Abbas from Muqatil, al-Dahhak, and Ali ibn Abi Talha, Ibn Ashur considers Ali ibn Abi Talha’s the soundest; al-Bukhari relied on it for glosses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r7.anchor: وأصحها رواية علي بن أبي طلحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r8.claim: Fabricators and obscuring transmitters used Ibn Abbas’s fame as cover to authenticate reports they circulated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r8.anchor: قد اتخذها الوضاعون والمدلسون ملجأ لتصحيح ما يروونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r9.speaker: أبو جحيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r9.claim: Abu Juhaifa asked Ali whether the family possessed revelation beyond the Quran; Ali swore they did not, except for understanding God grants a person of the Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r9.anchor: عن أبي جحيفة قال : قلت لعلي هل عندكم شيء من الوحي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r10.claim: Most tafsir reports ascribed to Ali are fabricated, except those with sound chains; Ibn Ashur cites the Abu Juhaifa report as evidence of Ali’s Quranic understanding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r10.anchor: وهنالك روايات تسند لعلي رضي الله عنه ، أكثرها من الموضوعات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r11.claim: Later Quran commentators followed different approaches and intellectual tastes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r11.anchor: ثم تلاحق العلماء في تفسير القرآن وسلك كل فريق مسلكا يأوي إليه وذوقا يعتمد عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r12.claim: The transmitted-report approach is associated first with Malik and also al-Dawudi; al-Tabari is its best-known representative in the available works.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r12.anchor: وأشهر أهل هذه الطريقة فيما هو بأيدي الناس محمد بن جرير الطبري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r13.claim: Some commentators used reasoned analysis, while many relied heavily on Israelite stories, causing fabricated material to proliferate in their books.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r13.anchor: وشغف كثير بنقل القصص عن الإسرائيليات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Atiyya both probe meanings, cite Arabic evidence and earlier exegetes; rhetoric and Arabic predominate for al-Zamakhshari, while law predominates for Ibn Atiyya, and both became major references.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p14/r14.anchor: يأتي بشواهدها من كلام العرب ويذكر كلام المفسرين
